xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5348: Composer: sending bare /pan fails with 404 'Missing an Overdeck command... Type /pan to list available commands'

plan.title: Composer: sending bare /pan fails with 404 'Missing an Overdeck command... Type /pan to list available commands'
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: Sending bare /pan in a conversation composer fails with HTTP 404 'Missing an Overdeck command after /pan. Type /pan to list available commands.' because resolveEntry in src/lib/composer-commands/parser.ts throws for an empty token list, and both message routes map unknown-command to 404. The error tells the operator to do what they just did. /pan help fails the same way because the CLI registry excludes Commander's implicit help. Separately, typing /pan and pressing Enter in the slash picker of a Claude Code conversation inserts /context, whose description contains 'expand'.
narratives.Proposal: The parser maps /pan, /pan help, /pan --help and /pan -h to a dashboard-owned COMPOSER_HELP_ENTRY. The router answers that entry before any policy or executor with a captured result (command '/pan help') whose output is built in-process from the manifest and the policy overlay: composer-runnable commands first, then every other top-level command grouped by manifest category as 'pan <syntax>'. The existing captured-result row renders it, so no contract or component change is needed. The slash picker gains a static /pan entry and ranks exact and label matches before description-only matches, so /pan + Enter picks /pan. Docs, changelog and the CI frontend subset are updated. Full detail: .pan/drafts/PAN-5348.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No new ComposerCommandResult kind and no change to CommandResultRow.tsx or isComposerCommandResult
- No per-command help for /pan help <verb>; it is rejected with the existing 'Unexpected token' error
- No change to the policy overlay (which commands run in the composer)
- No listing of subcommands; only top-level commands appear
- No edit to composer-commands.generated.ts, scripts/slash-commands-curation.json or the generator
- No fix for the case mismatch between the frontend /pan regex (case-insensitive) and the server's case-sensitive isComposerCommandMessage
- No --help support after a subcommand (/pan show --help still answers 422 unknown flag)
- The help list never spawns pan --help or any child process

autoDecisions.summary: Answer bare /pan on the server, not with a frontend shortcut
autoDecisions.rationale: Both message routes already intercept /pan before delivery, and MCP send_message and pan tell use the same routes, so one server fix covers every client and keeps the message out of the agent.

autoDecisions.summary: Reuse kind 'captured' for the help result
autoDecisions.rationale: The captured row already renders multi-line output with a 200 status; a new kind would need the contracts type, the strict isComposerCommandResult switch, statusSentence and the row to change together, and an unrecognized 200 body is silently treated as an acknowledged prompt.
pan --help prints a flat Commander list with no group headings, so the only grouping the CLI registry defines is the category assigned in scripts/slash-commands-curation.json.

autoDecisions.summary: List top-level commands only, with composer-runnable ones in a first section
autoDecisions.rationale: pan --help lists top-level commands; only 8 of 92 run in the composer and the rest answer 422, so separating them keeps the list truthful about what can be typed here.
Commander accepts all three help forms so operators type them by habit; per-command help is extra scope the issue did not ask for.

The issue asks that typing /pan use the picker; without ranking, /pan + Enter in a Claude Code conversation inserts /context because its description contains 'expand', so the keyboard path stays broken.

narrative.Action: Follow PRD Work Item 1 in .pan/drafts/PAN-5348.md: in src/lib/composer-commands/parser.ts export COMPOSER_HELP_ENTRY (id pan-help, path ['help'], display '/pan help', args/options/aliases empty, category Core) and HELP_TOKENS {'help','--help','-h'}; export expectedSyntax; in resolveEntry return the help entry with pathLength 0 for an empty token list and pathLength 1 when tokens[0] is a help token, before the manifest lookup; replace the unknown-command ternary with the single message 'Unknown Overdeck command "<token>". Type /pan to list available commands.' Do not touch the generated manifest or the policy overlay. Add the four parser tests named in the PRD.

items.title: Given each of '/pan', '/pan help', '/pan --help', '/pan -h' and '/pan   ', when parseOverdeckComposerCommand runs, then it returns entry.id 'pan-help' and argv ['help'] (parser.test.ts)

Given '/pan help start', when parsed, then it throws ComposerCommandParseError with code 'unknown-command', token 'start' and message 'Unexpected token "start" for /pan help. Expected syntax: /pan help.'

Given '/pan frobnicate', when parsed, then the thrown message equals 'Unknown Overdeck command "frobnicate". Type /pan to list available commands.' and grep for 'Missing an Overdeck command' in parser.ts returns no match

Build the grouped /pan help list in-process from the manifest and policy overlay

narrative.Action: Follow PRD Work Item 2: create src/lib/composer-commands/help.ts exporting buildComposerHelpOutput() and buildComposerHelpResult(). The output is exactly the format in the PRD: header 'Overdeck commands', a 'Run in this composer (type /pan <command>):' section listing every manifest entry whose resolvePolicy(path).mode is not 'terminal-only' with expectedSyntax, then 'Run in a terminal (type pan <command> in a shell):' followed by one section per manifest category (first-appearance order) of top-level (path.length === 1) terminal-only entries written as 'pan <syntax>', syntax column padded to the longest syntax capped at 36, and the footer 'Run pan <command> --help in a terminal for subcommands and options.' The result is a captured completed result with command '/pan help' and truncated false. Never spawn a process. Add help.test.ts with the five tests named in the PRD.
